subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Strategy, Teamwork, Leadership, and Lifetime Activity
essentialQuestion: How do strategy, leadership, and inclusion make activity work for everyone?

prompts.prompt: Name the movement cues for offensive and defensive space and explain what each one does.
Show, describe, or diagram inclusive design and lifetime activity options. A demonstration, a spoken description, and a drawing are equally valid.
Apply simple tactics and adjusting a plan in a new movement task at a challenge level you select. Control and cue use are assessed, not speed, distance, or count.
A made-up learner is struggling with roles, rotation, and officiating. Identify the likely cue or decision at fault, correct it, and explain why the correction helps.
Connect offensive and defensive space with conflict resolution and repair. Explain how one supports the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Design an inclusive small-sided game, then lead or officiate it for an adult or a group and review what you would change for access and fairness. A learner may instead officiate a scripted scenario or write and justify the design.
Describe one way you adapted a task so it worked for you, and one activity from this unit you would choose to do again. There is no wrong answer here.

adaptationChoices: Access supports may change equipment, distance, speed, force, duration, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. Using the adapted alternative is a full-credit path, never a reduced one.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change equipment, distance, speed, force, duration, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. Using the adapted alternative is a full-credit path, never a reduced one.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
